title: Storage Maintenance and Database Statistics
learningObjectives: Explain why database maintenance is scheduled.
Use ANALYZE to collect SQLite planner statistics.
Use PRAGMA optimize as an engine-specific maintenance entry point.
Recognize the storage and locking implications of maintenance operations.

understand.concept: Database maintenance keeps storage structures and planner statistics in a useful state as data changes. Maintenance tasks must be selected for the target engine and run with an awareness of workload impact.
understand.whyItMatters: Outdated statistics or fragmented storage can affect query planning and resource use, while poorly timed maintenance can compete with application traffic.
understand.analogy: A library periodically re-shelves books and updates its catalogue so items remain easy to find.
understand.analogyLimit: SQLite commands such as ANALYZE and PRAGMA optimize do not map one-to-one to maintenance commands in PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQL Server.

explain.narrative:
## Statistics and query planning
The optimizer estimates how many rows a predicate will match and compares possible plans. ANALYZE collects table and index statistics that can improve those estimates. SQLite stores statistics in internal tables such as sqlite_stat1.

## PRAGMA optimize
PRAGMA optimize is SQLite's recommended entry point for targeted optimization work. It may decide that analysis is useful based on database history and version; it does not necessarily perform work every time.

## Maintenance scheduling
Maintenance can consume CPU, disk I/O and locks. Schedule it based on workload and engine guidance, monitor duration and failures, and verify query plans after significant data changes. Never assume a maintenance command improves every query.

examples.title: Create an event table for maintenance examples
examples.code: CREATE TABLE ops21_events (event_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_type TEXT NOT NULL, event_day TEXT NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: Creates a table whose event_type column will be indexed for a common filter pattern.

examples.title: Generate a representative event set
examples.code: WITH RECURSIVE seq(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM seq WHERE n < 50) INSERT INTO ops21_events SELECT n, CASE WHEN n % 2 = 0 THEN 'login' ELSE 'payment' END, '2026-11-' || printf('%02d', (n % 28) + 1) FROM seq;
examples.explanation: Generates 50 deterministic sample rows. This is a small test fixture; production plan decisions require representative data volume and distribution.

examples.title: Create an index for event-type filtering
examples.explanation: Adds an index that the planner may use for event_type predicates. Every index adds storage and write-maintenance cost.

examples.title: Collect statistics and inspect the recorded table/index entry
examples.code: ANALYZE ops21_events; SELECT tbl, idx FROM sqlite_stat1 WHERE tbl = 'ops21_events' ORDER BY idx IS NULL, idx;
examples.explanation: Runs ANALYZE and reads the index-specific statistics entry from SQLite's statistics table. SQLite may not create a separate table-wide row when index statistics are available; exact statistics values are intentionally not hard-coded.

examples.title: Run SQLite's optimization entry point and verify source rows remain
examples.code: PRAGMA optimize; SELECT COUNT(*) AS event_rows FROM ops21_events;
examples.explanation: Runs PRAGMA optimize, which may perform targeted analysis depending on engine version and history, then verifies the table still contains 50 events. Maintenance should not change the logical business rows.

practise.guidedTask: Run ANALYZE and PRAGMA optimize. Inspect sqlite_stat1 and explain why its exact statistics values should not be used as a fixed expected output across every dataset.
practise.independentTask: Choose a frequently filtered table from a project. Propose an index, gather statistics, compare EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN before and after, and document write/storage trade-offs.
hints: Statistics help the optimizer estimate row counts.
ANALYZE gathers table and index statistics in SQLite.
PRAGMA optimize may do nothing when no work is needed.
Use representative data when comparing plans.
Maintenance consumes resources and should be scheduled.

questions.prompt: What does ANALYZE collect in SQLite?
options: Statistics used by the query planner
questions.answer: Statistics used by the query planner
questions.explanation: Statistics help the optimizer estimate candidate plan costs.

questions.prompt: Does PRAGMA optimize always change the database?
options: No; it may decide no optimization work is needed
Yes, it always rebuilds every index
Only when there are no tables
questions.answer: No; it may decide no optimization work is needed
questions.explanation: Its actions depend on database history and engine version.

questions.prompt: Why use representative data for plan testing?
options: Data volume and distribution influence optimizer choices
It guarantees a specific plan string
questions.answer: Data volume and distribution influence optimizer choices
questions.explanation: A tiny fixture can lead to a different plan from production.

questions.prompt: What is a cost of adding indexes?
questions.explanation: Indexes must be maintained as rows change.

questions.prompt: What should follow a major data or schema change?
options: Recheck plans and measure important workloads
questions.answer: Recheck plans and measure important workloads
questions.explanation: Plan and performance behaviour can change as the data changes.
